transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Well... I suppose I'm here about my eating. It's just... once I start eating those comfort foods, I try to tell myself, 'Maria, that is enough.' But... my hand just goes back to the pot anyway. It's like I just can’t make myself stop.
When you find yourself continuing to eat even though you want to stop, does it feel like you’ve lost control over your eating at those moments?
I suppose you could call it that... Like I just mentioned, I... I tell myself to quit, but it doesn't do any good. I just can't seem to make it stop.
Does this feeling of not being able to stop eating those foods cause you distress or affect your daily life in any way?

Well... I still get my things done. I go to Mass, and my choir practice... I take care of the house. But... I suppose if I have one of those afternoons, I might just stay in for the rest of the day. I don't really want to call anyone or... talk to anyone. It's just... well, it's a bit embarrassing, is all.
When you feel like you can't stop eating those comfort foods, would you say that you're eating a much larger amount of food than what most people would eat in a similar period of time?

Well... I suppose so. Sometimes, if it's an afternoon after choir, or... maybe after working out in the garden... I'll fix myself a plate of rice and beans, or some chicken stew. But then... I just keep going back for more. I guess by the time I finally stop, I've... well, I've eaten enough for two or three meals.
When you're eating those larger amounts of food, do you find yourself eating more quickly than normal, eating until you feel uncomfortably full, or eating even when you're not really hungry?

Well... I don't know about all of that. But I suppose... well, I've always been a slow eater, you see. My mother used to scold me for taking too long at the table. But when I get like this... I don't know. I just stand there by the kitchen counter, and... I eat fast. I hardly even taste it before I'm taking the next bite. It's just... fast.
When you're eating those larger amounts of food, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full or eating even when you're not really hungry?

Well... I suppose so. By the time I finally stop... my stomach just feels very tight. And heavy. I usually have to go sit in my recliner for a bit... maybe loosen my waistband. I just... well, I end up going past what feels comfortable. That's all.

When you're eating those larger amounts, does it happen in a short period of time, like within a couple of hours, and do you feel like you’re eating all of it in one go rather than spreading it out normally?
Well... I don't really know about the time. I'm not looking at a clock. I just... eat it while I'm standing there. I suppose it's all at once.
Do you usually eat alone during these times because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Well... I don't really know if I'd say I'm embarrassed. I just... I live alone, you see. My husband passed a few years back. So... I'm usually by myself anyway. I don't really think about it like that.
After eating like that, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, taking laxatives, or exercising more than usual?
No... I don't do anything like that. I just... sit in my chair and let my stomach settle. I certainly wouldn't make myself sick. And I'm much too old to be doing any heavy exercising.
Do you feel a lot of shame or guilt after these episodes of eating, and does it interfere with how you live your life, like keeping you from social activities or making you feel bad about yourself?

Well... yes, I suppose I do feel bad. Afterward. It's... well, I feel ashamed. And sad. Cooking and eating... it always meant family to me. Caring for my husband, having people over. Now... I just feel like I've turned it into something ugly. Something I wouldn't want the ladies at church to know about. So... yes, I feel bad.
How often would you say these episodes of eating this larger amount of food happen — like, how many times a week or month do they occur?

I suppose... most weeks. Maybe... once or twice a week. It's, well... it's been that way since my friend passed away. Usually just on those quiet afternoons. Like when I get back from choir... or after I finish up out in the garden. That's... that's about how often.
Would you say these episodes of eating happen at least once a week on average over the past three months?
Yes... I suppose so. It's been about three months now. Ever since my friend passed away.
